_comment: Performance budget (pipeline/README.md). The gate reads the preset the run used; `budgetPreset` is the preset the harness runs by default (the owner's choice, 2026-10-04: Low carries the 60 fps target on a low-spec laptop). Frame-time lines (p95Ms, p99Ms) are gated only in the environments listed in frameTimeGatedEnvs: everywhere else they are reported, not judged (no GPU in the cloud container). Draw calls and triangles are set below the owner's ceilings (150, 250k) because today's scene uses 35 and 47k on Low: a doubling must fail. `ticks` is the measured window per environment in simulation ticks (3600 is 60 s of play; the container's simulation runs at about 16 ticks/s in software, so 1800 ticks takes about two minutes there). `presetTicks` shortens the window where a preset is far slower in software (Medium and High draw shadows and relief at a few frames a second in the container, about 1.5 ticks/s, so 360 ticks keeps each run near four minutes); `perf-run.mjs --preset all` runs the four presets in turn (audit REN-15). `desktop` (G5) is the owner's desktop PC, unthrottled, where Ultra is measured at 3840×2160 (perf-desktop.mjs): its frame times are judged on Ultra only (`frameTimeGatedPresets`), against `envs.desktop.ultra` (PF3, owner 2026-10-17: the line sits at the baseline of 2026-10-17 so Ultra can't get slower, p95 6.5 and p99 9 ms; WebGL2's own, 7.2 and 11.5 in `envs.desktop.backends.webgl`, is PF3's reading of that, DECISIONS; the aim stays 4K at 240 Hz, 4.17 ms a frame, which that baseline misses on every map, KNOWN_ISSUES); `envs.<env>.<preset>` lines apply over every other line in that environment (perfMatrix.mjs budgetFor); Ultra's draw-call line is the owner's ceiling, as High's (G5: the post passes add about 15 full-screen draws, and Ultra measured 85 on Depot; gpuMemoryMB counts geometry and textures, not the render targets). `matrix` is what the gate runs (M76, audit CORE-03): every map in both modes on Low, and Extraction on Medium on the big maps, each only when the diff reaches it (pipeline/perfMatrix.mjs), and each combination runs once per back end listed (an entry's `backend`: `webgl`, the node renderer's WebGL2 back end, when absent, or `webgpu`); each has its own baseline, `baseline/<env><tag>.json` on the budget preset and `baseline/<env><tag>-<preset>.json` otherwise, where the tag is `-<map>` (not for Depot) then `-extraction` (not for Elimination). `maps` holds a map's own lines over the preset's (owner decision 4 of audit 2: map-scoped Medium budgets for Woodland and Neon Heights after M75's trims). `baselineMaxLag`: the gate warns, never fails, when a baseline's head is more commits behind HEAD than this (CORE-12). `backends.<id>` overrides lines per back end (`presets.<preset>`, then `maps.<map>.<preset>`, over the map's lines; WebGPU overhaul W6); empty today: both back ends hold the same lines outside the desktop's Ultra frame times. `triangles` is the scene's own; `dressingTriangles` (W6a) is the GPU dressing's (Woodland's grass and tree stand-ins on Medium and up), which Three counts at its caps whatever the cull keeps, so each preset's line is its caps (config/gpuDressing.ts: three triangles a blade slot, two a stand-in) plus 2 %. `mapIds` names each map the matrix and the run files call by a short name with its id in the game (map/maps.ts), for perf-run.mjs and the content toolkit's map checks (CT2); a map not listed is called by its id. Raise a line with a DECISIONS entry.
